value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for technical notes whose every claim says how it is known
value.lets_workers: Write and check technical notes, summaries and commit messages so every claim says how it is known: label each claim as measured here, read, verified, reported, designed or unverified with the evidence that label needs, rest conclusions only on measured, read or verified claims, reproduce reported numbers before relying on them, leave unmeasured values empty with a reason, append corrections instead of editing them away, and state the limits.

value.title: How claims are labeled, reproduced, corrected and audited
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: label-claims sorts every claim in a draft by how it is known and attaches the evidence each label needs.
reproduce-claim reruns the method behind a reported or old number before anything rests on it.
record-correction appends what was claimed, what was true and how the error was made.
audit-note, by a different worker or a person, checks labels, evidence, conclusions, absent values, corrections and limits.
rules: A status reachable without evidence will be reached without evidence: make evidence part of every measured claim.
Commit messages, summaries and status lines are claims too and take the same labels.
A record that keeps only the surviving claims teaches nothing about how the wrong ones were made.
Say what measured means in this note; a request reaching a probe is a lower bar than a tool working.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.category_reason: A fixed labeling vocabulary applied claim by claim.

labels.measured_here: Run in this work: the command, a digest of its output, the environment, the sample size and the time.
labels.read: Read from a source without running it: the source, the exact locator and the revision.
labels.verified: Checked against a primary source in this work: which source and when.
labels.reported: Measured or stated by someone else and not reproduced here: who, and whether a reproduction was tried.
labels.designed: Intent only; nothing built or measured.
labels.unverified: Tried and could not confirm: what was tried.

value.title: Reproducing a number before anything rests on it
rules: Rerun the stated method in a stated environment, and set the tolerance before rerunning.
State n. One run is one run.
Not reproduced means a correction, even when the new number looks better.
Could not run is unknown, never reproduced.
Hash the output so a later reader can tell the evidence did not change.

value.title: Comparing options without fooling yourself
rules: State the sample size for every option. Separating success rates near 100 and 75 percent at the usual 5 percent significance and 80 percent power takes about 27 cases per option; with fewer, report a tie and the counts.
Isolate shared state: a shared library or cache lets one option replay another's work.
Freeze the runner and environment during a comparison; changing them midway mixes several systems.
Record each command's own exit status; a pipe into a filter reports the filter's status, not the command's.
Credit a reuse only when the reused item existed before the run began.
Report every cost field for every option, and leave unmeasured fields empty with a reason.

deterministic_checks.why: A note is true only as of a date.
A claim measured here carries the command, a digest of its output, the environment, the sample size and the time.
A claim read from a source says exactly where.
A verified claim names the primary source it was checked against and when.
A reported claim says who reported it and whether it was reproduced.
An unverified claim says what was tried.
Every conclusion names the claims it rests on.
A conclusion rests on claims measured here, read from a cited source or verified, never on reported, designed or unverified ones.
An unmeasured value is listed with a reason instead of being written as zero.
A correction keeps what was claimed, what was true and how the error was made.
Every note says what it does not establish.
The note says what its measurements actually show, which is often a lower bar than the tool working.
